analysis.title: USA: Core CPI Above Expectations; Estimating 0.32% for September Core PCE
key_insights: Core CPI rose 0.33% m/m in September, above the 0.2% median forecast and GS's 0.24%. Y/Y core CPI was 2.56% vs GS 2.46% and median 2.5%.

Shelter drove the surprise. OER rose 0.35% m/m and contributed 12bp to core, about 5bp more than GS expected. The strength was concentrated in the Midwest (+0.68%, SA by GS), while the Northeast (+0.39%), West (+0.25%) and South (+0.14%) were roughly in line with GS's estimate of the underlying trend.
Rent rose 0.25% m/m and contributed about 3bp to core.
Travel services were firm. Lodging rose 2.0% m/m and airfares 1.2% m/m, together contributing 6bp to core.
New and used cars contributed 3bp to core, consistent with GS's expectation for a pickup in autos inflation.
Recreation was firm, driven by toys and games (+4.2% m/m, a volatile category), contributing about 3bp to core.
Headline CPI rose 0.65% m/m, roughly in line with expectations, on energy prices up 5.2% tied to the re-escalation of the conflict in Iran. Y/Y headline was 3.74% vs GS 3.70% and median 3.6%.

GS estimates September core PCE rose 0.32% m/m (vs 0.20% expected before the CPI release), or 3.09% y/y. The revision mainly reflects upside surprises in OER, hotels and recreation. Headline PCE is estimated at +0.49% m/m and +3.62% y/y.

The CPI report and the core PCE implication raise the probability of an October Fed hike. GS still expects the second hike in December. Tomorrow's PPI and Chairman Warsh's speech at the IMF annual meetings in Bangkok later this week will give more information on timing.
